      "observations": [
        "All 275 owned diff lines across six paths were read. LocalCopyHeaders already had its plural symbol name; the title does not establish a function rename. The isMove parameter and preference reads are removed from that helper. Common local copying selects dontPreserveOnCopy, while the historical EWS caller selects copy versus move before passing StringFields(dontPreserve). The helper gains fixed exclusions for offlineMsgSize, ewsId and uidOnServer in addition to storeToken and msgOffset, then appends caller exclusions.",
        "Accepted LocalCopyHeaders retains the five literal fixed keys and copies other string properties using the nsTArray exclusion lookup. Its existing flag carry-over remains separate from property selection. The accepted current protocol path is now ExchangeMessageCopyHandler: it selects the operation preference and passes the array into ExchangePerformMessageCreateFromCopy. The downstream handler clones that array and stores it by value; this later asynchronous ownership is not attributed to the original synchronous call. kExchangeIdProperty still maps to stored ewsId.",
        "StringFields returns owning nsCString elements and omits empty fields after skipping runs of SPACE, TAB, LF, FF and CR. Vertical tab and non-ASCII separators are not in its predicate. The new public comment says ASCII whitespace broadly, so preserve the implementation set rather than assuming Unicode or every ASCII whitespace character. The test directly compares arrays for eight empty/space/CRLF/TAB+FF/multibyte-word cases; it does not cover vertical tab or property copying. Its one new ASSERT_EQ(got, t.expected) lacks an explicit streamed message with case/expected behavior.",
        "The modified ParseIdentificationFields comment becomes a documentation block but retains mismatched braces/brackets and missing quotes in some examples. Its actual parser is unchanged here and still labels its RFC handling ad hoc. The reviewer malformed-ID concern was qualified as somewhat off-topic/IIRC; no new comma/no-space/missing-bracket handling follows from Done. The preference-removal aim in the summary is not implemented; accepted callers still read both preferences.",
        "Manual scope is the local scanner, typed nsTArray fields, caller context and copied-header identity. Exact token exclusion replaces padded substring searching. No source or instruction was edited, and no C++/GTest, copy/move, database or message operation ran. No runtime failure is inferred from an omitted assertion message or the untested delimiter cases.",
        "The original source-only discussion-pending marker is historical and is resolved here. Full Bug2014903 current 0–12 was read once by B for the three-part family and reused with its exact original identity/time. C collected the complete own D287506 timeline, one actual inline body and one actual Old/New summary pair.",
        "The summary edit adds why the responsibility moves upward: lower callers do not always know copy versus move context. The source selects the preference in callers and removes the isMove argument from LocalCopyHeaders. The stated longer-term preference-removal aim remains unimplemented; accepted callers still read both preferences.",
        "The malformed Message-ID/References suggestion is explicitly qualified as somewhat off-topic/IIRC. The changed source converts documentation here but does not alter ParseIdentificationFields. Its current implementation remains an ad-hoc space splitter with paired-angle stripping, so Done is not proof of new comma, no-space or missing-bracket handling. The separate StringFields test covers only its explicit field-splitting cases.",
        "Historical formatting task failures with no detected defect, later build completion, additional diff updates and the final ongoing/failed-build landing remain separate. No current lint pass, copy/move execution or parser test result is inferred. The accepted asynchronous array clone is a later source boundary, with C retained as original reader of the surrounding consumer."
